title.raw: 卷4上 世祖紀上 Volume 4a Annals: Shizu 1 (Emperor Taiwu)

sentences.zh: 世祖太武皇帝，諱燾，太宗明元皇帝之長子也，母曰杜貴嬪。

translations.literal: Shizu, Emperor Taiwu — taboo name Tao — was Taizong Emperor Mingyuan's eldest son. His mother was Lady Du, Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, Emperor Taiwu, bore the taboo name Tao. He was the eldest son of Taizong, Emperor Mingyuan; his mother was Lady Du, Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 天賜五年生於東宮，體貌瓌異，太祖奇而悅之，曰：「成吾業者，必此子也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianci he was born in the Eastern Palace. His form and bearing were extraordinary; Taizu marveled and was pleased, saying: "He who will complete my enterprise must be this boy."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianci he was born in the Eastern Palace. His bearing was strikingly unusual; Taizu wondered at him and said, "The one who will finish what I began is this child."

sentences.zh: 」泰常七年四月，封泰平王，五月，為監國。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year of Taichang, fourth month, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Taiping; fifth month, he became regent of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the seventh year of Taichang he was made Prince of Taiping; in the fifth month he was appointed regent.

sentences.zh: 太宗有疾，命帝總攝百揆，聰明大度，意豁如也。

translations.literal: Taizong fell ill and ordered the Emperor to oversee all government affairs. He was intelligent and magnanimous, his mind open and at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong fell ill, he put the heir in charge of government. The prince was bright and broad-minded, untroubled in spirit.

sentences.zh: 八年十一月壬申，[1]即皇帝位，大赦天下。

translations.literal: Eighth year, eleventh month, day renshen, [1] he ascended the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the eighth year, on the renshen day, [1] he took the throne and granted amnesty to the empire.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，追尊皇妣為密皇后，進司徒長孫嵩爵為北平王，司空奚斤為宜城王，藍田公長孫翰為平陽王，其餘普增爵位各有差。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: his late mother was posthumously honored as Empress Mi; Chancellor of State Changsun Song was advanced to Prince of Beiping, Minister of Works Xi Jin to Prince of Yicheng, Duke of Lantian Changsun Han to Prince of Pingyang; the rest received general advancement of noble rank, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he raised his late mother to Empress Mi; Changsun Song, Chancellor of State, became Prince of Beiping; Xi Jin, Minister of Works, Prince of Yicheng; Changsun Han, Duke of Lantian, Prince of Pingyang; and the rest were promoted in rank, each as deserved.

sentences.zh: 於是除禁錮，釋嫌怨，開倉庫，賑窮乏，河南流民相率內屬者甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon prohibitions were lifted, grudges released, granaries opened, and the destitute relieved; very many displaced people south of the Yellow River came in groups to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He ended arbitrary detention, cleared old grievances, opened the storehouses, and aided the poor; refugees south of the Yellow River flocked inward in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 始光元年春正月丙寅，安定王彌薨。

translations.literal: Shiguang year 1, spring, first month, day bingyin: Prince of Anding Mi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shiguang, on the bingyin day of the first month of spring, Prince of Anding Mi died.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲辰，東巡，幸大寧。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiachen: the court toured east and visited Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the jiachen day, the emperor toured east to Daning.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 八月，蠕蠕率六萬騎入雲中，殺掠吏民，攻陷盛樂宮。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the Rouran led sixty thousand horsemen into Yunzhong, killing and plundering officials and people, and captured Shengle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Rouran brought sixty thousand horsemen into Yunzhong, slaughtered and looted the people, and took Shengle Palace.

sentences.zh: 赭陽子尉普文率輕騎討之，虜乃退走。

translations.literal: Ziyangzi Wei Puwen led light cavalry against them; the barbarians then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Puwen, Lord of Ziyang, led light horse against them and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔平陽王長孫翰等擊蠕蠕別帥，破之，殺數千人，獲馬萬餘匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others to strike a Rouran sub-chief; they defeated him, killed several thousand, and captured more than ten thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, and others to attack a Rouran sub-chief; they broke him, killed several thousand men, and took more than ten thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 語在蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the Rouran treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is given in the treatise on the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 九月，大簡輿徒，治兵於東郊，部分諸軍五萬騎，將北討。

translations.literal: Ninth month: a great muster of chariots and foot soldiers; troops were drilled at the eastern suburb and the armies were divided—fifty thousand horsemen—to campaign north.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he mustered chariots and infantry, drilled the army at the eastern suburb, and arrayed fifty thousand horsemen for a northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 冬十有二月，遣平陽王長孫翰等討蠕蠕。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month: Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others were sent to campaign against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter he sent Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, and others against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 車駕次祚山，蠕蠕北遁，諸軍追之，大獲而還。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted at Zuoshan; the Rouran fled north and the armies pursued, taking great booty before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted at Zuoshan; the Rouran fled north, the armies pursued, won a great haul, and returned.

sentences.zh: 是年，劉義符為其臣徐羨之等所廢殺，立義符弟義隆。

translations.literal: That year Liu Yifu was deposed and killed by his ministers Xu Xianzhi and others; his younger brother Yilong was installed.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Yifu was overthrown and killed by his ministers Xu Xianzhi and others, who set up his younger brother Yilong.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月己卯，車駕至自北伐，以其雜畜班賜將士各有差。

translations.literal: Year 2, spring, first month, day jimao: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign and distributed captured livestock to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the jimao day of the first month of spring, the court returned from the northern expedition and divided the captured herds among officers and men, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 二月，慕容渴悉隣反於北平，攻破郡治，太守與守將擊敗之。

translations.literal: Second month: Murong Kesilin rebelled at Beiping, broke the commandery seat; the governor and defending generals attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Murong Kesilin rebelled in Beiping and stormed the commandery seat; the governor and garrison commanders defeated him.

sentences.zh: 三月丙辰，尊保母竇氏曰保太后。

translations.literal: Third month, day bingchen: the wet-nurse Lady Dou was honored as Dowager Protector.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day of the third month the wet-nurse Lady Dou was honored as Dowager Protector.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以北平王長孫嵩為太尉，平陽王長孫翰為司徒，宜城王奚斤為司空。

translations.literal: Day dingsi: Prince of Beiping Changsun Song was made Grand Commandant, Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han Chancellor of State, Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day Changsun Song, Prince of Beiping, became Grand Commandant; Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, Chancellor of State; and Xi Jin, Prince of Yicheng, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 庚申，營故東宮為萬壽宮，起永安、安樂二殿，臨望觀、九華堂。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: the former Eastern Palace was converted into Wanshou Palace; the Yong'an and Anle halls were raised, the Linwang Observatory and Jiuhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day the old Eastern Palace was made Wanshou Palace; the Yong'an and Anle halls were built, with the Linwang Observatory and Jiuhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 初造新字千餘，詔曰：「在昔帝軒，創制造物，乃命倉頡因鳥獸之跡以立文字。

translations.literal: More than a thousand new characters were first devised. An edict said: "In former times Emperor Xuan of the Yellow lineage created and fashioned things; he ordered Cang Jie to establish writing from the traces of birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand new characters were devised for the first time. An edict declared: "Long ago the Yellow Emperor fashioned the world and ordered Cang Jie to fix writing from the tracks of birds and beasts."

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，隨時改作，故篆隸草楷，並行於世。

translations.literal: From that time onward scripts were altered with the age; thus seal, clerical, cursive, and regular forms have all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: "Since then each age has changed the script, so seal, clerical, cursive, and regular forms have all been in use."

sentences.zh: 然經歷久遠，傳習多失其真，故令文體錯謬，會義不愜，非所以示軌則於來世也。

translations.literal: Yet because long transmission has lost the true forms, the written style is confused and the meeting of meanings unsatisfactory—not how to show a standard to later ages.
translations.idiomatic: "But long transmission has blurred the true forms, so texts are corrupt and meanings fail to meet—this is no way to set a standard for posterity."

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，名不正則事不成，此之謂矣。

translations.literal: Confucius said: when names are not correct, affairs do not succeed—this is what he meant.
translations.idiomatic: "Confucius said that when names are not correct, affairs do not succeed. He spoke of this."

sentences.zh: 今制定文字，世所用者，頒下遠近，永為楷式。」

translations.literal: Now writing is fixed for what the age uses; it is to be promulgated far and near and made the permanent model."
translations.idiomatic: "Now we fix the characters the age shall use, promulgate them far and near, and make them the lasting model forever."

sentences.zh: 夏四月，詔龍驤將軍步堆、謁者僕射胡覲使於劉義隆。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: an edict that General of Dragon Celerity Bu Dui and Master of Ceremonies Hu Gu were to go as envoys to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he ordered Bu Dui, General of Dragon Celerity, and Hu Gu, Master of Ceremonies, as envoys to Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔天下十家發大牛一頭，運粟塞上。

translations.literal: Fifth month: an edict that throughout the realm every ten households were to furnish one large ox to haul grain to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he decreed that every ten households in the empire must supply one large ox to haul grain to the border.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，永安、安樂二殿成，丁卯，大饗以落之。

translations.literal: Autumn, ninth month: the Yong'an and Anle halls were completed; day dingmao, a great feast marked their completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn the Yong'an and Anle halls were finished; on the dingmao day a great feast celebrated them.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，治兵於西郊。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: troops were drilled at the western suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the army was drilled at the western suburb.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，車駕北伐，平陽王長孫翰等絕漠追之，蠕蠕北走。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage campaigned north; Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han and others crossed the desert in pursuit and the Rouran fled north.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day the emperor marched north; Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang, and others crossed the desert in pursuit and the Rouran fled north.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 是年，赫連屈丐死，子昌僭立。

translations.literal: That year Helian Ququ died; his son Chang presumptuously succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year Helian Ququ died and his son Chang seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月壬申，車駕至自北伐。

translations.literal: Year 3, spring, first month, day renshen: the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the renshen day of the first month of spring, the court returned from the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 班軍實以賜將士，行、留各有差。

translations.literal: Captured goods were distributed to the officers and soldiers; those who marched and those who remained each received according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Booty was divided among the troops; those who had marched and those who had stayed behind were rewarded each as earned.

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐遣使朝貢，請討赫連昌。

translations.literal: Qifu Chipo sent envoys with tribute and requested permission to campaign against Helian Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipo sent tribute and asked leave to attack Helian Chang.

sentences.zh: 二月，起太學於城東，祀孔子，以顏淵配。

translations.literal: Second month: the Imperial Academy was founded east of the city; Confucius was sacrificed to, with Yan Yuan as associate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the Imperial Academy was founded east of the city; Confucius was honored and Yan Yuan paired with him.

sentences.zh: 夏五月辛卯，中山公元纂進爵為王，南安公元素復先爵常山王。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day xinmao: Duke of Zhongshan Yuan Zuan was advanced to prince; Duke of Nan'an Yuan Su had his former title Prince of Changshan restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on the xinmao day, Yuan Zuan, Duke of Zhongshan, was raised to princely rank; Yuan Su, Duke of Nan'an, had his former title Prince of Changshan restored.

sentences.zh: 六月，幸雲中舊宮，謁陵廟；

translations.literal: Sixth month: the court visited the old palace at Yunzhong and paid respects at the imperial tombs;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the emperor visited the old palace at Yunzhong and the ancestral tombs;

sentences.zh: 西至五原，田於陰山；

translations.literal: west to Wuyuan, hunting on Yinshan;
translations.idiomatic: west to Wuyuan, hunting on Yinshan;

sentences.zh: 東至和兜山。

translations.literal: east to Hedou Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: east to Hedou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，築馬射臺于長川，帝親登臺觀走馬；

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: a horse-shooting platform was built on Changchuan; the Emperor personally mounted the platform to watch the running horses;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn a horse-shooting terrace was built on Changchuan; the emperor mounted it to watch the races;

sentences.zh: 王公諸國君長馳射，中者賜金錦繒絮各有差。

translations.literal: princes, dukes, and the chieftains of the various states galloped and shot; those who hit the mark received gold, brocade, and silk floss, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: princes, dukes, and foreign chieftains rode and shot; hits were rewarded with gold, brocade, and silk, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 八月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Eighth month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝以屈丐既死，諸子相攻，九月，遣司空奚斤率義兵將軍封禮、雍州刺史延普襲蒲坂，宋兵將軍周幾率洛州刺史于栗磾襲陝城。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Ququ was dead and his sons were attacking one another, in the ninth month sent Minister of Works Xi Jin with General of Righteous Troops Feng Li and Yanzhou Inspector Yan Pu to strike Puban, and Song general Zhou Ji with Luozhou Inspector Yu Liben to strike Shancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ququ was dead and his sons were at war, in the ninth month the emperor sent Xi Jin, Minister of Works, with Feng Li, General of Righteous Troops, and Yan Pu, governor of Yanzhou, against Puban, and Zhou Ji of Song with Yu Liben, governor of Luozhou, against Shancheng.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁巳，車駕西伐，幸雲中，臨君子津。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dingsi: the imperial carriage campaigned west, visited Yunzhong, and came to Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the dingsi day, the emperor marched west, came to Yunzhong, and halted at Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 會天暴寒，數日冰結。

translations.literal: Heaven suddenly turned bitter cold; within days the river froze solid.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden bitter cold fell; within days the river was ice.

sentences.zh: 十有一月戊寅，帝率輕騎二萬襲赫連昌，壬午，至其城下，徙萬餘家而還。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day wuyin: the Emperor led twenty thousand light horse in a surprise attack on Helian Chang; day renchen, he reached below the city walls and moved more than ten thousand households back.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the wuyin day, the emperor led twenty thousand light cavalry in a surprise raid on Helian Chang; on the renchen day he reached the walls and carried off more than ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 語在昌傳。

translations.literal: The account is in the Chang treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The account is given in the treatise on Chang.

sentences.zh: 至祚山，班所虜獲以賜將士各有差。

translations.literal: At Zuoshan the captives were distributed to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuoshan the captives were divided among the troops, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 奚斤未至蒲坂，昌守將赫連乙升棄城西走。

translations.literal: Xi Jin had not yet reached Puban when Chang's defending general Helian Yisheng abandoned the city and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Before Xi Jin reached Puban, Chang's defender Helian Yisheng abandoned the city and fled west.

sentences.zh: [2]昌弟助興守長安，乙升復與助興自長安西走安定。

translations.literal: [2] Chang's younger brother Zhuxing held Chang'an; Yisheng joined Zhuxing and they fled west from Chang'an toward Anding.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Chang's brother Zhuxing held Chang'an; Yisheng joined him and they fled west from Chang'an toward Anding.

sentences.zh: 奚斤遂入蒲坂。

translations.literal: Xi Jin then entered Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin then entered Puban.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，詔斤西據長安。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: an edict that Xi Jin was to press west and hold Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he ordered Xi Jin to advance west and secure Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 秦雍氐、羌皆叛昌詣斤降。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all rebelled against Chang and came to Xi Jin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all turned from Chang and surrendered to Xi Jin.

sentences.zh: 武都氐王楊玄及沮渠蒙遜等皆遣使內附。

translations.literal: Yang Xuan, Di king of Wudu, and Juqu Mengxun and others all sent envoys to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan, Di king of Wudu, Juqu Mengxun, and others all sent envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月乙酉，車駕至自西伐，賜留臺文武生口、繒帛、馬牛各有差。

translations.literal: Year 4, spring, first month, day yiyou: the imperial carriage returned from the western campaign and bestowed on the civil and military officials who remained at the capital captives, silk, horses, and oxen, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, on the yiyou day of the first month of spring, the court returned from the western expedition and rewarded the officials who had stayed at the capital with captives, silk, horses, and oxen, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 從人在道多死，其能到都者纔十六七。

translations.literal: Very many of those who followed the march died on the road; barely sixteen or seventeen in ten reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Many who had marched died on the road; scarcely one in six reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 己亥，行幸幽州。

translations.literal: Day jihai: the court traveled to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day the emperor went to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 赫連昌遣其弟平原公定率眾二萬向長安。

translations.literal: Helian Chang sent his younger brother Duke of Pingyuan Ding with twenty thousand men toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang sent his brother Ding, Duke of Pingyuan, with twenty thousand men toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，乃遣就陰山伐木，大造攻具。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he sent men to Yinshan to fell timber and build siege engines on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor sent men to Yinshan to fell timber and build siege engines in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 二月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Second month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 三月丙子，遣高涼王禮鎮長安。

translations.literal: Third month, day bingzi: Prince of Gaoliang Li was sent to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day of the third month Prince of Gaoliang Li was sent to garrison Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 詔執金吾桓貸造橋於君子津。

translations.literal: An edict that Bearer of the Golden Mace Huan Dai was to build a bridge at Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Huan Dai, Bearer of the Golden Mace, to build a bridge at Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，廣平王連薨。

translations.literal: Day dingchou: Prince of Guangping Lian died.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day Prince of Guangping Lian died.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁未，詔員外散騎常侍步堆、謁者僕射胡覲等使於劉義隆。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day dingwei: an edict that Supernumerary Palace Attendant Bu Dui, Master of Ceremonies Hu Gu, and others were to go as envoys to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the dingwei day, he ordered Bu Dui, Supernumerary Palace Attendant, Hu Gu, Master of Ceremonies, and others as envoys to Liu Yilong.

sentences.zh: 是月，治兵講武，分諸軍，司徒長孫翰、廷尉長孫道生、宗正娥清三萬騎為前驅，常山王素、太僕兵堆、將軍元太毗步兵三萬為後繼，南陽王伏真、執金吾桓貸、將軍姚黃眉步兵三萬部攻城器械，將軍賀多羅精騎三千為前候。

translations.literal: That month troops were drilled and martial arts rehearsed; the armies were divided—Chancellor Changsun Han, Court Director Changsun Daosheng, and Director of Imperial Clan E Qing, thirty thousand horsemen as vanguard; Prince of Changshan Su, Grand Steward Bing Dui, and General Yuan Taipi, thirty thousand foot as rear guard; Prince of Nanyang Fuzhen, Bearer of the Golden Mace Huan Dai, and General Yao Huangmei, thirty thousand foot to manage siege engines; General He Duoluo, three thousand picked horse as scouts.
translations.idiomatic: That month the army was drilled: Changsun Han, Chancellor, Changsun Daosheng, Court Director, and E Qing, Director of the Imperial Clan, led thirty thousand horse as vanguard; Prince of Changshan Su, Grand Steward Bing Dui, and General Yuan Taipi, thirty thousand foot as rear; Prince of Nanyang Fuzhen, Huan Dai, Bearer of the Golden Mace, and General Yao Huangmei, thirty thousand foot with siege train; General He Duoluo, three thousand elite horse as scouts.

sentences.zh: 五月，車駕西討赫連昌。

translations.literal: Fifth month: the imperial carriage campaigned west against Helian Chang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor marched west against Helian Chang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，濟君子津。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: he crossed Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day he crossed Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 三城胡酋鵲子相率內附。

translations.literal: The Hu chieftain Quezi of Sancheng led his people inward in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Quezi, Hu chieftain of Sancheng, led his people to submit.

sentences.zh: 帝次拔隣山，築城，舍輜重，以輕騎三萬先行。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted at Balin Mountain, built a fort, left the baggage train, and with thirty thousand light horse went ahead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor halted at Balin Mountain, built a camp, left the baggage, and pressed on with thirty thousand light horse.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，至于黑水，帝親祈天告祖宗之靈而誓眾焉。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: he reached the Black Water; the Emperor personally prayed to Heaven and reported to the spirits of the ancestors, swearing the host.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day he reached the Black Water; the emperor prayed to Heaven and invoked the ancestral spirits before the army.

sentences.zh: 六月甲辰，昌引眾出城，大破之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiachen: Chang led his host out of the city and was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the sixth month Chang led his army out and was utterly broken.

sentences.zh: 事在昌傳。

translations.literal: The matter is in the Chang treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The account is in the treatise on Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌將麾下數百騎西南走，奔上邽，諸軍乘勝追至城北，死者萬餘人，臨陣殺昌弟河南公滿及其兄子蒙遜。

translations.literal: Chang with several hundred horsemen under his command fled southwest to Shanggui; the armies pursued in victory to below the city walls; more than ten thousand were killed in battle; on the field Chang's younger brother Duke of Henan Man and his brother's son Mengxun were slain.
translations.idiomatic: Chang fled southwest to Shanggui with a few hundred horse; the armies pursued to the walls and killed more than ten thousand; in the fighting Chang's brother Man, Duke of Henan, and his nephew Mengxun were slain.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，昌尚書僕射問至拔城，夜將昌母出走。

translations.literal: At dusk Chang's Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wen Zhiba seized the city; that night he took Chang's mother and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Wen Zhiba, Chang's Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, held the city; that night he fled with Chang's mother.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，車駕入城，虜昌羣弟及其諸母、姊妹、妻妾、宮人萬數，府庫珍寶車旗器物不可勝計，擒昌尚書王買、薛超等及司馬德宗將毛脩之、秦雍人士數千人，獲馬三十餘萬匹，牛羊數千萬。

translations.literal: Day yisi: the imperial carriage entered the city; Chang's younger brothers and all their mothers, sisters, wives, concubines, and palace women—tens of thousands; the treasuries' gems, chariots, banners, and utensils beyond counting; Chang's Masters of Writing Wang Mai, Xue Chao, and others were captured, with Mao Xiuzhi, general to Sima Dezong, and several thousand men of Qin and Yong; more than three hundred thousand horses and tens of millions of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day the emperor entered the city. He took Chang's brothers, their mothers, sisters, wives, concubines, and palace women by the tens of thousands; treasure, chariots, banners, and goods beyond count; Chang's Masters of Writing Wang Mai and Xue Chao; Mao Xiuzhi, general to Sima Dezong; and several thousand men of Qin and Yong; more than three hundred thousand horses and tens of millions of cattle and sheep.

sentences.zh: 以昌宮人及生口、金銀、珍玩、布帛班賚將士各有差。

translations.literal: Chang's palace women, captives, gold and silver, rare objects, silk, and cloth were distributed to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's palace women, captives, gold, silver, treasures, and cloth were divided among the troops, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 昌弟平原公定拒司空奚斤於長安城，娥清率騎五千討之，西走上邽。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Duke of Pingyuan Ding resisted Minister of Works Xi Jin at Chang'an; E Qing with five thousand horse campaigned against him; he fled west to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Ding, Duke of Pingyuan, held Chang'an against Xi Jin; E Qing with five thousand horse drove him west to Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，班師，留常山王素、執金吾桓貸鎮統萬。

translations.literal: Day xinyou: the army withdrew; Prince of Changshan Su and Bearer of the Golden Mace Huan Dai were left to garrison Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day the army withdrew; Prince of Changshan Su and Huan Dai, Bearer of the Golden Mace, were left to garrison Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己卯，築壇於祚嶺，戲馬馳射，賜射中者金錦繒絮各有差。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jimao: a platform was built on Zuoling; horses were raced and archery practiced; those who hit the mark received gold, brocade, and silk floss, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jimao day, a terrace was raised on Zuoling for racing and archery; hits were rewarded with gold, brocade, and silk, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕寇雲中，聞破赫連昌，懼而還走。

translations.literal: The Rouran raided Yunzhong; hearing that Helian Chang was broken, they feared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran raided Yunzhong; hearing of Chang's defeat, they fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 八月壬子，車駕至自西伐，飲至策勳，告於宗廟，班軍實以賜留臺百僚，各有差。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day renzi: the imperial carriage returned from the western campaign; a feast celebrated merit and report was made at the ancestral temple; captured goods were distributed to the officials who had remained at the capital, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day of the eighth month the court returned from the west; a feast honored the victors and the ancestral temple was told; booty was divided among the capital officials, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 九月丁酉，安定民舉城歸降。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day dingyou: the people of Anding raised the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the ninth month the people of Anding surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 冬十有一月，以氐王楊玄為都督荊梁益寧四州諸軍事、假征南大將軍、梁州刺史、南秦王。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: Di king Yang Xuan was made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Jing, Liang, Yi, and Ning provinces, Acting General Who Conquers the South, Inspector of Liangzhou, and King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Yang Xuan, Di king, was made commander of all armies in Jing, Liang, Yi, and Ning, acting General Who Conquers the South, inspector of Liangzhou, and King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 十有二月，行幸中山，守宰貪污免者十數人。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: the court traveled to Zhongshan; more than ten district magistrates were dismissed for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the emperor went to Zhongshan; more than ten magistrates were removed for graft.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 復所過田租之半。

translations.literal: Half the field tax along the route was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Half the land tax along the route was remitted.

sentences.zh: 神䴥元年春正月，以天下守令多行非法，精選忠良悉代之。

translations.literal: Shenju year 1, spring, first month: because prefects and magistrates throughout the realm often acted unlawfully, the loyal and able were carefully selected to replace them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenju, first month of spring, because magistrates throughout the empire often broke the law, trustworthy men were chosen to replace them.

sentences.zh: 辛未，京兆王黎薨。

translations.literal: Day xinwei: Prince of Jingzhao Li died.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day Prince of Jingzhao Li died.

sentences.zh: 二月，改元。

translations.literal: Second month: the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 赫連昌退屯平涼。

translations.literal: Helian Chang withdrew and encamped at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang withdrew to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 司空奚斤進軍安定，將軍丘堆為昌所敗，監軍侍御史安頡出戰，擒昌。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xi Jin advanced on Anding; General Qiu Dui was defeated by Chang; Supervising Censor An Gu went out to battle and captured Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin, Minister of Works, advanced on Anding; General Qiu Dui was beaten by Chang; Supervising Censor An Gu took the field and captured Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌餘眾立昌弟定為王，走還平涼。

translations.literal: Chang's remaining host installed Chang's younger brother Ding as king and fled back to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's remnant forces made his brother Ding king and fled back to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 三月癸酉，詔侍中古弼迎赫連昌。

translations.literal: Third month, day guiyou: an edict that Palace Attendant Gu Bi was to welcome Helian Chang.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day of the third month he ordered Palace Attendant Gu Bi to escort Helian Chang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，弼等以昌至于京師。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: Bi and others brought Chang to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day Bi brought Chang to the capital.

sentences.zh: 司空奚斤追定於平涼馬髦嶺，為定所擒。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xi Jin pursued Ding to Mama Ridge at Pingliang and was captured by Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin pursued Ding to Mama Ridge near Pingliang and was taken by Ding.

sentences.zh: 丘堆先守輜重在安定，聞斤敗，棄甲東走蒲坂。

translations.literal: Qiu Dui first guarded the baggage train at Anding; hearing that Xi Jin was defeated, he cast off armor and fled east to Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Dui had been guarding the baggage at Anding; when he heard Xi Jin was beaten, he threw off his armor and fled east to Puban.

sentences.zh: 帝聞大怒，詔安頡斬堆。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and was greatly angry; an edict that An Gu was to execute Qiu Dui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered An Gu to execute Qiu Dui.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，赫連定遣使朝貢，帝詔諭之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Helian Ding sent envoys with tribute; the Emperor issued instructions to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Helian Ding sent tribute; the emperor sent him a written reply.

sentences.zh: 壬子，西巡。

translations.literal: Day renzi: toured west.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day the court toured west.

sentences.zh: 戊午，田于河西。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: hunted on the west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day he hunted west of the river.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下。

translations.literal: General amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He granted amnesty to the empire.

sentences.zh: 南秦王楊玄遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: King of Southern Qin Yang Xuan sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuan, King of Southern Qin, sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月丁酉，并州胡酋卜田謀反伏誅，餘眾不安。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dingyou: Bingzhou Hu chieftain Bu Tian plotted rebellion and was executed; the remainder were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day of the sixth month Bu Tian, Hu chieftain of Bingzhou, plotted rebellion and was put to death; his followers were uneasy.

sentences.zh: 詔淮南公王倍斤鎮慮虒，撫慰之。

translations.literal: An edict that Duke of Huainan Wang Beijin was to garrison Lüsi and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wang Beijin, Duke of Huainan, to garrison Lüsi and reassure them.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，行幸長川。

translations.literal: Day jiayin: traveled to Changchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day he went to Changchuan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 八月，東幸廣寧，臨觀溫泉。

translations.literal: Eighth month: toured east to Guangning and viewed the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he toured east to Guangning and visited the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 以太牢祭黃帝、堯、舜廟。

translations.literal: With the great offering he sacrificed at the temples of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He offered the great sacrifice at the temples of the Yellow Emperor, Yao, and Shun.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕大檀遣子將萬餘騎入塞。

translations.literal: Rouran Datun sent his son with more than ten thousand horsemen into the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Datun of the Rouran sent his son with more than ten thousand horse across the border.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 上郡休屠胡酋金崖率部內屬。

translations.literal: Jinyai, chieftain of the Xiutu Hu of Shang commandery, led his tribe inward in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Jinyai, Xiutu Hu chieftain of Shang commandery, led his people to submit.

sentences.zh: 九月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Ninth month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上洛巴渠泉午觸等萬餘家內附。

translations.literal: Quan Wu and others of the Ba chieftains of Shangluo, more than ten thousand households, submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wu and other Ba chiefs of Shangluo, more than ten thousand households, came in submission.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲辰北巡。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiachen: toured north.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiachen day, he toured north.

sentences.zh: 壬子，田于牛川。

translations.literal: Day renzi: hunted at Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day he hunted at Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆淮北鎮將王仲德遣步騎二千餘入寇濟陽、陳留。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongde, frontier general of Liu Yilong north of the Huai, sent more than two thousand foot and horse to raid Jiyang and Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongde, Liu Yilong's general north of the Huai, sent more than two thousand foot and horse to raid Jiyang and Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 是月，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: That month: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: That month the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 閏月辛巳，義隆又遣將王玄謨、兗州刺史竺靈秀步騎二千人寇滎陽，將襲虎牢。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day xinsi: Yilong again sent Generals Wang Xuemo and Yanzhou Inspector Zhu Lingxiu with two thousand foot and horse to raid Xingyang, intending to strike Hubao.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the xinsi day, Yilong again sent Wang Xuemo and Zhu Lingxiu, governor of Yanzhou, with two thousand foot and horse against Xingyang, meaning to take Hubao.

sentences.zh: 豫州遣軍逆擊走之。

translations.literal: Yuzhou sent troops to meet and attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou sent troops to meet them and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 上郡屠各隗詰歸率萬餘家內屬。

translations.literal: Kui Zhi, chieftain of the Tuge of Shang commandery, led more than ten thousand households inward in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Zhi, Tuge chieftain of Shang commandery, led more than ten thousand households to submit.

sentences.zh: 定州丁零鮮于臺陽、翟喬等二千餘家叛入西山，劫掠郡縣，州軍討之，失利。

translations.literal: Xianyu Taiyang, Zhai Qiao, and others of the Dingling at Dingzhou, more than two thousand households, rebelled into the western hills, plundering commanderies and districts; the provincial army campaigned against them and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Dingzhou, Xianyu Taiyang, Zhai Qiao, and other Dingling, more than two thousand households, rebelled into the western hills and looted the districts; the provincial army attacked and lost.

sentences.zh: 詔鎮南將軍、壽光侯叔孫建擊之。

translations.literal: An edict that General Who Guards the South, Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian, was to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Shusun Jian, General Who Guards the South and Marquis of Shouguang, to strike them.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，行幸河西，大校獵。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: traveled to Hexi and held a great hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he went to Hexi for a great hunt.

sentences.zh: 十有二月甲申，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day jiashen: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the twelfth month the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是歲，皇子晃生。

translations.literal: That year the imperial son Huang was born.
translations.idiomatic: That year the prince Huang was born.

sentences.zh: 乞伏熾磐死，子暮末僭立。

translations.literal: Qifu Chipo died; his son Mumi presumptuously succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Chipo died and his son Mumi seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，赫連定弟酒泉公儁自平涼來奔。

translations.literal: Year 2, spring, first month: Helian Ding's younger brother Duke of Jiuquan Jun came in flight from Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month of spring, Ding's brother Jun, Duke of Jiuquan, fled from Pingliang to the court.

sentences.zh: 丁零鮮于臺陽等歸罪，詔赦之。

translations.literal: Xianyu Taiyang and others pleaded guilty; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Taiyang and his band pleaded guilty and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 二月，上黨李禹聚眾殺太守，自稱無上王，署置將帥。

translations.literal: Second month: Li Yu of Shangdang gathered a host, killed the governor, styled himself King Without Superior, and appointed generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Li Yu of Shangdang raised a force, killed the governor, called himself King Without Superior, and set up commanders.

sentences.zh: 河內守將擊破之。

translations.literal: The defending general of Henei attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander of Henei defeated him.

sentences.zh: 禹亡走入山，為人執送，斬之。

translations.literal: Yu fled into the mountains; men seized him and sent him in; he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fled into the hills, was seized and sent in, and was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，治兵于南郊。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: troops were drilled at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the army was drilled at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，車駕北伐，以太尉、北平王長孫嵩，衞尉、廣陵公樓伏連留守京師，從東道與長孫翰等期會於賊庭。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: the imperial carriage campaigned north; Grand Commandant, Prince of Beiping Changsun Song, and Commandant of Guards, Duke of Guangling Lou Fulian, were left to guard the capital; by the eastern route he was to join Changsun Han and others at the enemy's court.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day the emperor marched north, leaving Changsun Song, Grand Commandant and Prince of Beiping, and Lou Fulian, Commandant of Guards and Duke of Guangling, at the capital; by the eastern road he was to meet Changsun Han at the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 五月丁未，次于沙漠，舍輜重，輕騎兼馬，至栗水，蠕蠕震怖，焚燒廬舍，絕跡西走。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day dingwei: halted in the desert, left the baggage train, light horse with spare mounts reached Lishui; the Rouran were terrified, burned their lodges, and vanished west.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day of the fifth month he halted in the desert, left the baggage, and with light horse and remounts reached Lishui; the Rouran were terrified, burned their camps, and fled west without trace.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 是月，赫連定來侵統萬，東至侯尼城而還。

translations.literal: That month Helian Ding came to raid Tongwan, went east to Houni city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That month Helian Ding raided Tongwan, reached Houni city in the east, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，車駕東轅。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial carriage turned east.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the court turned east.

sentences.zh: 至黑山，校數軍實，班賜王公將士各有差。

translations.literal: At Heishan the armies' stores were reviewed and distributed to princes, dukes, and officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: At Heishan the booty was counted and divided among princes, dukes, and troops, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝以東部高車屯巳尼陂，詔左僕射安原率騎萬餘討之。

translations.literal: Eighth month: because the eastern Gaoche were encamped at Sini marsh, an edict that Left Vice Director An Yuan was to lead more than ten thousand horse against them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, because eastern Gaoche were camped at Sini marsh, he ordered An Yuan, Left Vice Director, with more than ten thousand horse against them.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully set forth in the Rouran treatise.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the treatise on the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，振旅凱旋于京師，告於宗廟。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: the army returned in triumph to the capital and reported at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter the army returned in triumph to the capital and reported to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 列置新民於漠南，東至濡源，西暨五原、陰山，竟三千里。

translations.literal: New subjects were arrayed south of the desert, east to Ruyuan, west to Wuyuan and Yinshan, three thousand li in all.
translations.idiomatic: New subjects were settled south of the desert from Ruyuan in the east to Wuyuan and Yinshan in the west, three thousand li in all.

sentences.zh: 詔司徒平陽王長孫翰、尚書令劉潔，左僕射安原、侍中古弼鎮撫之。

translations.literal: An edict that Chancellor Prince of Pingyang Changsun Han, Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Jie, Left Vice Director An Yuan, and Palace Attendant Gu Bi were to garrison and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Changsun Han, Prince of Pingyang and Chancellor, Liu Jie, Director of the Masters of Writing, An Yuan, Left Vice Director, and Gu Bi, Palace Attendant, to garrison and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 十有一月，西巡狩，田于河西，至祚山而還。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: toured west on a hunt, hunted on Hexi, reached Zuoshan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he hunted west in Hexi, reached Zuoshan, and returned.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲子，行幸雲中。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jiazi: traveled to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the jiazi day, he went to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 敕勒萬餘落叛走。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Tiele households rebelled and fled.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Tiele households rebelled and fled.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書封鐵追討滅之。

translations.literal: An edict that Director of the Masters of Writing Feng Tie was to pursue and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Feng Tie of the Masters of Writing to pursue and destroy them.

sentences.zh: 五月戊戌，詔曰：「夫士之為行，在家必孝，處朝必忠，然後身榮於時，名揚後世矣。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuxu, edict: "A gentleman's conduct: at home he must be filial, at court loyal—then his person is honored in his age and his name praised by later generations.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day of the fifth month an edict declared: "A man's conduct should be filial at home and loyal at court; only then is he honored in his time and remembered after."

sentences.zh: 近遣尚書封鐵翦除亡命，其所部將士有盡忠竭節以殞軀命者，今皆追贈爵號；

translations.literal: Recently Director Feng Tie cut down fugitives; among the officers and soldiers under his command were those who gave their utmost loyalty and perished in the service—now all are posthumously enfeoffed with noble rank;
translations.idiomatic: "Lately Feng Tie of the Masters of Writing destroyed fugitives. Officers and men who died in loyal service shall now receive posthumous ranks;

sentences.zh: 或有蹈鋒履難以自效者，以功次進位；

translations.literal: there were those who braved blades and hardship to offer themselves—advancement in rank according to merit;
translations.idiomatic: those who braved blades and hardship shall be advanced by merit;

sentences.zh: 或有故違軍法私離幢校者，以軍法行戮。

translations.literal: there were those who deliberately violated military law and privately left their banners—execution by military law.
translations.idiomatic: those who deliberately broke military law and left their units shall die by military law.

sentences.zh: 夫有功蒙賞，有罪受誅，國之常典，不可暫廢。

translations.literal: Merit receives reward, crime receives punishment—the constant rule of the state cannot for a moment be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: "Merit is rewarded and crime punished—the state's constant rule must not lapse even for a moment."

sentences.zh: 自今以後，不善者可以自改。

translations.literal: From now on the unworthy may reform themselves.
translations.idiomatic: "From now on the unworthy may reform themselves."

sentences.zh: 其宣敕內外，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: Proclaim this inside and outside so all may hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: "Let this be proclaimed within and without until all have heard."

sentences.zh: 」六月，詔平南大將軍、假丹陽王太毗屯于河上，以司馬楚之為安南大將軍、琅邪王，屯潁川。

translations.literal: " Sixth month: an edict that General Who Pacifies the South, Acting Prince of Danyang Taipi, was to garrison on the river; Sima Chuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the South, Prince of Langye, and garrisoned Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he ordered Taipi, General Who Pacifies the South and acting Prince of Danyang, to garrison on the river, and made Sima Chuzhi General Who Pacifies the South and Prince of Langye, garrisoning Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己亥，詔曰：「昔太祖撥亂，制度草創，太宗因循，未遑改作，軍國官屬，至乃闕然。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jihai, edict: "In former times Taizu raised order amid chaos and institutions were first drafted; Taizong followed along and had no leisure to revise; military and civil offices even stood vacant.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the seventh month of autumn an edict said: "Taizu, raising order from chaos, first drafted institutions; Taizong followed but had no time to revise them, and military and civil posts even stood empty."

sentences.zh: 今諸征鎮將軍、王公仗節邊遠者，聽開府辟召；

translations.literal: Now generals on campaign, princes and dukes bearing credentials on distant frontiers, are permitted to open offices and recruit;
translations.idiomatic: "Now campaigning generals and princes and dukes with credentials on distant frontiers may open offices and recruit;

sentences.zh: 其次，增置吏員。

translations.literal: next, increase the number of clerks.
translations.idiomatic: next, increase clerical staff."

sentences.zh: 」庚子，詔大鴻臚卿杜超假節、都督冀定相三州諸軍事、行征南大將軍、太宰，進爵為王，鎮鄴，為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: " Day gengzi: Director of the Grand Messenger Office Du Chao was given credentials, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Xiang provinces, Acting General Who Conquers the South, Grand Preceptor, advanced to prince, garrisoned Ye, and made coordinator of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day Du Chao, Director of the Grand Messenger Office, received credentials as commander of armies in Ji, Ding, and Xiang, acting General Who Conquers the South and Grand Preceptor, was raised to princely rank, garrisoned Ye, and coordinated all armies.

sentences.zh: 八月，清河羣盜殺太守。

translations.literal: Eighth month: bandits in Qinghe killed the governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month bandits in Qinghe killed the governor.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆將到彥之，自清水入河，泝流西行。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong's general Dao Yanzhi entered the river from Qingshui and sailed upstream west.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yanzhi, general to Liu Yilong, entered the Yellow River from Qingshui and sailed upstream west.

sentences.zh: 帝以河南兵少，詔攝四鎮。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Henan had few troops, ordered the four garrisons taken under central command.
translations.idiomatic: Because Henan had few troops, the emperor put the four frontier garrisons under central command.

sentences.zh: 乃治兵，將西討。

translations.literal: Thereupon troops were drilled for a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He then drilled the army for a western expedition.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，到彥之遣將渡河攻冶坂，冠軍將軍安頡督諸軍擊破之，斬首五千餘級，投水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: Dao Yanzhi sent generals across the river to attack Yebai; Champion General An Gu directed the armies, defeated them, beheaded more than five thousand, and very many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day Yanzhi sent generals across the river against Yebai; An Gu, Champion General, led the armies, broke them, took more than five thousand heads, and drowned many more.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，行幸南宮，獵于南山。

translations.literal: Day jiaxu: traveled to Nangong and hunted on Nanshan.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day he went to Nangong and hunted on Nanshan.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔征西大將軍長孫道生屯于河上。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: an edict that General Who Conquers the West Changsun Daosheng was to garrison on the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day he ordered Changsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the West, to garrison on the river.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，赫連定遣弟謂以代寇鄜城，平西將軍、始平公隗歸等率諸軍討之，擒賊將王卑，殺萬餘人，謂以代遁走。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day jichou: Helian Ding sent his younger brother Wei Yi to raid Fucheng on behalf of Dai; General Who Pacifies the West, Duke of Shiping Wei Gui and others led the armies against them, captured the bandit general Wang Bei, killed more than ten thousand, and Wei Yi fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day of the ninth month Ding sent his brother Wei Yi to raid Fucheng for Dai; Wei Gui, General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Shiping, and others attacked, took the rebel general Wang Bei, killed more than ten thousand, and Wei Yi fled.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，立密皇太后廟于鄴。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the temple of Empress Mi was established at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day the temple of Empress Mi was founded at Ye.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，行幸統萬，遂征平涼。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: traveled to Tongwan and then campaigned against Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day he went to Tongwan and marched on Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 冬十月庚申，到彥之、王仲德沿河置守，還保東平。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day gengshen: Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde set guards along the river and withdrew to defend Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengshen day of the tenth month of winter Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde posted guards along the river and fell back to Dongping.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，冠軍將軍安頡濟河，攻洛陽，丙子，拔之，擒義隆將二十人，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Day yihai: Champion General An Gu crossed the river and attacked Luoyang; day bingzi, took it, captured twenty of Yilong's generals, and beheaded five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day An Gu, Champion General, crossed the river and attacked Luoyang; on the bingzi day he took it, captured twenty of Yilong's generals, and beheaded five thousand.

sentences.zh: 時河北諸軍會于七女津，彥之恐軍南度，遣將王蟠龍泝流欲盜官船，征南大將軍杜超等擊破，斬之。

translations.literal: At that time the armies of Hebei gathered at Qinv Ford; Yanzhi feared a southern crossing and sent General Wang Panlong upstream to seize government boats; Du Chao, General Who Conquers the South, and others defeated and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Hebei gathered at Qinv Ford; fearing a southern crossing, Yanzhi sent Wang Panlong upstream to seize government boats; Du Chao, General Who Conquers the South, and others defeated and killed him.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，安頡平虎牢，義隆司州刺史尹沖墜城死。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: An Gu pacified Hubao; Yilong's Inspector of Sizhou Yin Chong fell from the wall and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day An Gu took Hubao; Yin Chong, Yilong's inspector of Sizhou, fell from the wall and died.

sentences.zh: 十有一月乙酉，車駕至平涼。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day yiyou: the imperial carriage reached Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the eleventh month the court reached Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 先是，赫連定將數萬人東禦於鄜城，留其弟上谷公社于、廣陽公度洛孤城守。

translations.literal: Earlier Helian Ding with tens of thousands of men had gone east to hold Fucheng; he left his younger brother Duke of Shanggu Sheyu and Duke of Guangyang Duluo to guard the city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ding had gone east to Fucheng with tens of thousands; he left his brothers Sheyu, Duke of Shanggu, and Duluo, Duke of Guangyang, to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 帝至平涼，登北原，使赫連昌招諭之，社于不降。

translations.literal: The Emperor reached Pingliang, mounted the north plateau, and had Helian Chang summon them; Sheyu did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reached Pingliang, mounted the north plateau, and had Helian Chang summon them; Sheyu refused.

sentences.zh: 詔安西將軍古弼等擊安定，攻平涼。

translations.literal: An edict that General Who Pacifies the West Gu Bi and others were to attack Anding and assault Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gu Bi, General Who Pacifies the West, and others to attack Anding and besiege Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 定聞之，棄鄜城，入于安定，自率步騎三萬從鶉觚原將救平涼，與弼相遇，弼擊之，殺數千人，乃還走。

translations.literal: Ding heard, abandoned Fucheng, entered Anding, and himself led thirty thousand foot and horse from Chunqu plain to relieve Pingliang; he met Bi, Bi struck him, killed several thousand, and Ding turned back in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Ding heard, abandoned Fucheng, entered Anding, and led thirty thousand foot and horse from Chunqu plain to relieve Pingliang; he met Bi, who struck him, killed several thousand, and Ding fled back.

sentences.zh: 詔諸軍四面圍之。

translations.literal: An edict that the armies were to surround on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the armies to invest the city on all sides.

sentences.zh: 甲午，壽光侯叔孫建、汝陰公長孫道生濟河，到彥之、王仲德從清入濟，東走青州，義隆兗州刺史竺靈秀棄須昌，南奔湖陸。

translations.literal: Day jiawu: Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian and Duke of Runan Changsun Daosheng crossed the river; Dao Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde went from Qing into Ji and fled east to Qingzhou; Zhu Lingxiu, Yilong's governor of Yanzhou, abandoned Xuchang and fled south to Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day Shusun Jian, Marquis of Shouguang, and Changsun Daosheng, Duke of Runan, crossed the river; Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde fled east from Qing and Ji to Qingzhou; Zhu Lingxiu, Yilong's governor of Yanzhou, abandoned Xuchang and fled south to Hulu.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，定乏水，引眾下原，詔武衞將軍丘眷擊之，定眾大潰，死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: Ding lacked water and led his host down from the high ground; an edict that Martial Guard General Qiu Juan was to strike him; Ding's host was utterly routed and more than ten thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day Ding ran short of water and led his men down from the heights; the emperor ordered Qiu Juan, Martial Guard General, to strike; Ding's army broke and more than ten thousand died.

sentences.zh: 定中重創，單騎遁走。

translations.literal: Ding was gravely wounded and fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was badly wounded and fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 獲定弟丹陽公烏視拔、武陵公禿骨及公侯百餘人。

translations.literal: Captured Ding's younger brother Duke of Danyang Wushiba, Duke of Wuling Tugu, and more than a hundred dukes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: They took Ding's brother Wushiba, Duke of Danyang, Tugu, Duke of Wuling, and more than a hundred dukes and marquises.

sentences.zh: 是日，諸將乘勝進軍，遂取安定。

translations.literal: That day the generals pressed the victory and advanced; Anding was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: That day the generals pressed the victory and took Anding.

sentences.zh: 定從兄東平公乙升棄城奔長安，劫掠數千家，西奔上邽。

translations.literal: Ding's cousin Duke of Dongping Yisheng abandoned the city and fled to Chang'an, plundering several thousand households, then fled west to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's cousin Yisheng, Duke of Dongping, abandoned the city, fled to Chang'an, plundered several thousand households, and fled west to Shanggui.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，叔孫建大破竺靈秀於湖陸，殺獲五千餘人。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: Shusun Jian utterly defeated Zhu Lingxiu at Hulu, killing and capturing more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day Shusun Jian broke Zhu Lingxiu at Hulu and killed or captured more than five thousand.

sentences.zh: 己亥，帝幸安定，獲乞伏熾磐質子及定車旗，簿其生口、財畜，班賜將士各有差。

translations.literal: Day jihai: the Emperor visited Anding, took Qifu Chipo's hostage and Ding's chariots and banners, registered captives and livestock, and distributed to the officers and soldiers, each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day the emperor visited Anding, took Qifu Chipo's hostage and Ding's chariots and banners, tallied captives and herds, and divided them among the troops, each as earned.

sentences.zh: 庚子，帝自安定還臨平涼，遂掘塹圍守之。

translations.literal: Day gengzi: the Emperor returned from Anding to Pingliang and dug trenches to invest the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day he returned from Anding to Pingliang and dug trenches to besiege it.

sentences.zh: 行幸紐城，安慰初附，赦秦雍之民，賜復七年。

translations.literal: Traveled to Niucheng, comforted those newly submitted, pardoned the people of Qin and Yong, and granted seven years' remission of levies.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Niucheng, reassured the newly submitted, pardoned the people of Qin and Yong, and remitted levies for seven years.

sentences.zh: 定隴西守及將士數千人來降。

translations.literal: Defenders and officers and soldiers of Longxi, several thousand, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand defenders and soldiers of Longxi surrendered.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，冠軍將軍安頡率諸軍攻滑臺。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: Champion General An Gu led the armies to attack Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day An Gu, Champion General, led the armies against Huatai.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王司馬楚之破劉義隆將於長社。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Sima Chuzhi defeated Liu Yilong's general at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chuzhi, Prince of Langye, defeated a general of Liu Yilong at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，封壽光侯叔孫建為丹陽王。

translations.literal: On renyin Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian was enfeoffed as Prince of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Shusun Jian, Marquis of Shouguang, was made Prince of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 十有二月丁卯，定弟社于、度洛孤面縛出降，平涼平，收其珍寶。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day dingmao: Ding's younger brothers Sheyu and Duluo Gugu came bound in surrender; Pingliang was pacified and their treasures were seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingmao, Ding's brothers Sheyu and Duluo Gugu surrendered bound; Pingliang fell and their treasures were taken.

sentences.zh: 定長安、臨晉、武功守將皆奔走，關中平。

translations.literal: The garrison commanders of Chang'an, Linjin, and Wugong all fled; Guanzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders of Chang'an, Linjin, and Wugong all fled; Guanzhong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 壬申，車駕東還，留巴東公延普等鎮安定。

translations.literal: On renshen the imperial carriage returned east, leaving Duke of Badong Yanpu and others to garrison Anding.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the court turned east, leaving Yanpu, Duke of Badong, and others to hold Anding.

sentences.zh: 是歲，馮跋死，弟文通僭立。

translations.literal: That year Feng Ba died and his brother Wentong seized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: That year Feng Ba died and his brother Wentong usurped rule.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月壬午，車駕次于木根山，大饗羣臣，賜布帛各有差。

translations.literal: Year 4, spring, first month, day renwu: the imperial carriage halted at Mugen Mountain, held a great feast for the ministers, and distributed cloth and silk, each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, first month of spring, on renwu the court halted at Mugen Mountain, feasted the ministers, and gave cloth and silk by rank.

sentences.zh: 丙申，劉義隆將檀道濟、王仲德從清水救滑臺，丹陽王叔孫建、汝陰公長孫道生拒之，道濟等不敢進。

translations.literal: On bingshen Liu Yilong's generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde came from Qingshui to relieve Huatai; Prince of Danyang Shusun Jian and Duke of Yiyin Changsun Daosheng barred them, and Daoji and the others did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde of Liu Yilong came from Qingshui to save Huatai; Shusun Jian, Prince of Danyang, and Changsun Daosheng, Duke of Yiyin, blocked them and they did not advance.

sentences.zh: 是月，乞伏慕末為赫連定所滅。

translations.literal: That month Qifu Mumo was destroyed by Helian Ding.
translations.idiomatic: That month Qifu Mumo was destroyed by Helian Ding.

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉，安頡、司馬楚之平滑臺，擒義隆將朱脩之、李元德及東郡太守申謨。

translations.literal: Second month, day xinyou: An Gu and Sima Chuzhi pacified Huatai and captured Yilong's generals Zhu Xiuzhi and Li Yuande and Administrator of Dongjun Shen Mo.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou of the second month An Gu and Sima Chuzhi took Huatai and captured Zhu Xiuzhi, Li Yuande, and Shen Mo, governor of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，車駕還宮，飲至策勳，告於宗廟，賜留臺百官各有差，戰士賜復十年。

translations.literal: On guiyou the imperial carriage returned to the palace, held a feast celebrating merit, reported at the ancestral temple, rewarded the capital officials each according to rank, and granted soldiers ten years' tax exemption.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the court returned to the capital, feasted the victors, reported to the ancestral temple, rewarded the capital officials, and exempted soldiers from levies for ten years.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，行幸南宮。

translations.literal: On dingchou he traveled to the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he went to the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 定州民飢，詔啟倉以賑之。

translations.literal: The people of Ding province were hungry; an edict opened the granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Ding province was in famine; granaries were opened for relief.

sentences.zh: 義隆將檀道濟、王仲德東走，諸將追之，至歷城而還。

translations.literal: Yilong's generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde fled east; the generals pursued them to Licheng and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde fled east; pursuers reached Licheng and turned back.

sentences.zh: 三月庚戌，冠軍將軍安頡獻義隆俘萬餘人，甲兵三萬。

translations.literal: Third month, day gengxu: Champion General An Gu presented more than ten thousand of Yilong's captives and thirty thousand suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu of the third month An Gu, Champion General, presented more than ten thousand captives and thirty thousand suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 夏五月庚寅，行幸雲中。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month, day gengyin: traveled to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, on gengyin, he went to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 六月，赫連定北襲沮渠蒙遜，為吐谷渾慕璝所執。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Helian Ding raided north against Juqu Mengxun and was seized by Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Helian Ding raided Juqu Mengxun in the north and was captured by Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 閏月乙未，蠕蠕國遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, day yimao: the Rouran state sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on yimao, the Rouran sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔散騎侍郎周紹使于劉義隆。

translations.literal: An edict that Attendant Cadet Zhou Shao was envoy to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Attendant Cadet Zhou Shao to Liu Yilong as envoy.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己酉，行幸河西，起承華宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiyou: traveled to Hexi and began the Chenghua Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jiyou, he went to Hexi and began Chenghua Palace.

sentences.zh: 八月乙酉，沮渠蒙遜遣子安周入侍。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day yiyou: Juqu Mengxun sent his son Anzhou to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou of the eighth month Juqu Mengxun sent his son Anzhou to court.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾慕璝遣使奉表，請送赫連定。

translations.literal: Murong Mugui of Tuyuhun sent envoys with a memorial requesting to hand over Helian Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Mugui sent envoys asking to deliver Helian Ding.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以慕璝為大將軍、西秦王。

translations.literal: On jichou Mugui was made Grand General and King of Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Mugui was made Grand General and King of Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 九月癸丑，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day guichou: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guichou, the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 庚申，加太尉長孫嵩柱國大將軍，特進、左光祿大夫崔浩為司徒，征西大將軍長孫道生為司空。

translations.literal: On gengshen Grand Tutor Changsun Song was given the additional title Grand General with Pillar of State; Cui Hao, Special Advance and Left Grand Master of the Palace, was made Chancellor; Changsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the West, was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Changsun Song, Grand Tutor, received the added rank Grand General with Pillar of State; Cui Hao became Chancellor; Changsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the West, became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔兼太常李順持節拜河西王沮渠蒙遜為假節，加侍中，都督涼州及西域羌戎諸軍事、行征西大將軍、太傅、涼州牧、涼王。

translations.literal: On renhai an edict that Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies Li Shun, bearing credentials, was to invest Juqu Mengxun, King of Hexi, as Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies with staff, Commander of Liangzhou and all military affairs of the Western Regions and Qiang and Rong, Acting General Who Conquers the West, Grand Tutor, Governor of Liangzhou, and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On renhai Li Shun, Concurrent Grand Master of Ceremonies, was sent with credentials to invest Juqu Mengxun as King of Liang with full western command.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔曰：「頃逆命縱逸，方夏未寧，戎車屢駕，不遑休息。

translations.literal: On renshen an edict said: "Recently rebels have run wild; midsummer is not yet calm; war-chariots have been driven again and again without leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen an edict declared: "Rebels have lately run wild; midsummer is not yet calm; the army has marched again and again without rest."

sentences.zh: 今二寇摧殄，士馬無為，方將偃武修文，遵太平之化，理廢職，舉逸民，拔起幽窮，延登儁乂，昧旦思求，想遇師輔，雖殷宗之夢板築，罔以加也。

translations.literal: Now the two foes are destroyed and troops and horses are at ease; we shall lay down arms and cultivate letters, follow the transformation of great peace, put neglected offices in order, raise reclusive men, lift up the obscure and poor, advance the eminent and able, and at dawn seek and think—longing to meet teachers and aides—as the Yin house's dream of the plank road could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Now both enemies are gone and the host is idle; we will sheathe arms, restore civil order, revive abandoned posts, call out the hidden, and seek worthy counselors from dawn—surpassing even the Yin king's dream of worthy men in the wild."

sentences.zh: 訪諸有司，咸稱范陽盧玄、博陵崔綽、趙郡李靈、河間邢穎、勃海高允、廣平游雅、太原張偉等，皆賢儁之冑，冠冕州邦，有羽儀之用。

translations.literal: Inquiry was made of all offices; all praised Fan Yang Lu Xuan, Boling Cui Chuo, Zhao commandery Li Ling, Hejian Xing Ying, Bohai Gao Yun, Guangping You Ya, Taiyuan Zhang Wei, and others—all eminent scions and the ornament of their provinces, fit for ceremonial display.
translations.idiomatic: All offices named Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Cui Chuo of Boling, Li Ling of Zhao, Xing Ying of Hejian, Gao Yun of Bohai, You Ya of Guangping, Zhang Wei of Taiyuan, and others—men of talent and standing in their commands."

sentences.zh: 詩不云乎，『鶴鳴九臯，聲聞于天』，庶得其人，任之政事，共臻邕熙之美。

translations.literal: Does the Odes not say, 'The crane cries from the deep marsh, its voice heard in heaven'? We hope to obtain such men, employ them in government, and together reach the beauty of universal harmony.
translations.idiomatic: As the Odes says, 'The crane cries from the nine marshes, its voice heard in heaven'—may we find such men for office and share in ordered peace."

sentences.zh: 易曰：『我有好爵，吾與爾縻之。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'I have fine rank; I will tie it to you.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, 'I have fine rank; I will bind it to you.'"

sentences.zh: 』如玄之比，隱跡衡門、不耀名譽者，盡敕州郡以禮發遣。

translations.literal: ' Men like Xuan who hide in their lanes and do not display their fame—all provinces and commanderies are to send them forth with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xuan who live obscure without seeking fame—every province and commandery shall summon them with full ritual."

sentences.zh: 」遂徵玄等及州郡所遣，至者數百人，皆差次敍用。

translations.literal: " Xuan and the others and those sent by the provinces arrived—several hundred in all—and were appointed in due order.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and the rest, with those the provinces sent—several hundred in all—were ranked and appointed."

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊寅，詔司徒崔浩改定律令。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day wuyin: an edict that Chancellor Cui Hao was to revise the laws and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on wuyin, he ordered Chancellor Cui Hao to revise the laws.

sentences.zh: 行幸漠南。

translations.literal: Traveled to the southern desert.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the southern desert.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙辰，北部敕勒莫弗庫若于，率其部數萬騎，驅鹿數百萬，詣行在所，帝因而大狩以賜從者，勒石漠南，以記功德。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day bingchen: Mo Fu Kuruyu of the northern Tiele led his tribe, tens of thousands of horse, driving several million deer to the imperial halt; the Emperor therefore held a great hunt to reward the followers, inscribed a stone in the southern desert, and recorded the merit.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen of the eleventh month Kuruyu, Mo Fu of the northern Tiele, brought tens of thousands of horse and millions of deer to the camp; the emperor held a great hunt for his followers and set up a stone in the desert to record the deed.

sentences.zh: 宜城王奚斤，坐事降爵為公。

translations.literal: Prince of Yicheng Xi Jin was demoted to duke for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin, Prince of Yicheng, was reduced to duke for an offense.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁丑，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day dingchou: the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou of the twelfth month the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 延和元年春正月丙午，尊保太后為皇太后，立皇后赫連氏，立皇子晃為皇太子，謁于太廟，大赦，改年。

translations.literal: Yanhe year 1, spring, first month, day bingwu: the Guardian Empress was honored as Empress Dowager; Lady Helian was made empress; Prince Huang was made crown prince; the ancestral temple was visited; general amnesty; the era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanhe, first month of spring, on bingwu the Guardian Empress became Empress Dowager, Lady Helian empress, Prince Huang crown prince; the temple was visited, amnesty granted, and the reign title changed.

sentences.zh: 己巳，詔曰：「朕以眇身，獲奉宗廟，思闡洪基，廓清九服。

translations.literal: On jisi an edict said: "With my slight person I have received the ancestral temple, thinking to expand the great foundation and clear the nine domains.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi an edict said: "With this slight person I have received the ancestral shrine, intent on broadening the foundation and pacifying the realm."

sentences.zh: 遭值季運，天下分崩。

translations.literal: We met a declining age and the realm split apart.
translations.idiomatic: We met a declining age and the empire fell apart."

sentences.zh: 是用屢征，罔或寧息，自始光至今，九年之間，戎車十舉。

translations.literal: Therefore campaigns were repeated without rest; from Shiguang to now, in nine years the war-chariot has gone forth ten times.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns followed without pause—from Shiguang until now, in nine years the army marched ten times."

sentences.zh: 羣帥文武，荷戈被甲，櫛風沐雨，蹈履鋒刃，與朕均勞。

translations.literal: Commanders civil and military bore spears and armor, combed wind and washed rain, trod blades, and shared toil with Us.
translations.idiomatic: Generals and ministers bore arms, braved wind and rain, walked among blades, and shared our labor."

sentences.zh: 賴神祇之助，將士宣力，用能摧折強豎，克翦大憝。

translations.literal: Relying on the spirits' aid and the officers' and soldiers' exertion, We were able to break the strong and cut down the great foe.
translations.idiomatic: By the spirits' help and the troops' strength we broke the strong and destroyed the great enemy."

sentences.zh: 兵不極武，而二寇俱滅；

translations.literal: Arms did not reach their utmost and both foes were destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: Arms were not pushed to excess, yet both enemies perished;"

sentences.zh: 師不違律，而遐方以寧。

translations.literal: the army did not violate discipline and distant regions were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: the army kept discipline and distant lands were calm."

sentences.zh: 加以時氣和洽，嘉瑞並降，遍於郡國，不可勝紀，豈朕一人，獨應此祐，斯亦羣后協同之所致也。

translations.literal: Moreover the seasons were harmonious and auspicious omens came down together throughout the commanderies and districts beyond counting—how could We alone receive this blessing? It is also what the ministers achieved in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons were mild and good omens beyond count filled the commands—could We alone deserve this? It came from the ministers acting as one."

sentences.zh: 公卿因茲，稽諸天人之會，請建副貳。

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers therefore, aligning with the meeting of Heaven and man, requested establishment of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: The dukes and ministers, reading Heaven and man together, asked that the heir be set."

sentences.zh: 夫慶賞之行，所以褒崇勳舊，旌顯賢能，以永無疆之休，其王公將軍以下，普增爵秩，啟國承家，修廢官，舉儁逸，蠲除煩苛，更定科制，務從輕約，除故革新，以正一統。

translations.literal: The practice of reward and favor is to exalt old merit, display the able, and secure endless blessing; princes, dukes, generals, and all below were broadly raised in noble rank, founded states and inherited houses, restored abolished offices, raised eminent recluses, remitted burdensome levies, revised statutes, strove for lightness and simplicity, abolished the old and established the new, and rectified unity.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards should honor past service and display talent for lasting peace; princes, dukes, generals, and all below were raised in rank, states founded, offices restored, the worthy called out, harsh taxes cut, laws revised for simplicity, the old replaced and unity set right."

sentences.zh: 羣司當深思效績，直道正身，立功立事，無或懈怠，稱朕意焉。」

translations.literal: All offices should deeply consider effecting merit, keep to the straight way and correct the person, establish achievement and affairs, and not slacken—fitting Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: Every office must seek real achievement, walk uprightly, build lasting work, and not slacken—so We intend."

sentences.zh: 二月丙子，行幸南宮。

translations.literal: Second month, day bingzi: traveled to the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi of the second month he went to the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 三月丁未，追贈夫人賀氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Third month, day dingwei: Lady He was posthumously honored as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei of the third month Lady He was posthumously made empress.

sentences.zh: 壬申，西秦王吐谷渾慕璝，送赫連定於京師。

translations.literal: On renshen Murong Mugui, King of Western Qin, sent Helian Ding to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Mugui, King of Western Qin, sent Helian Ding to the capital.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，大簡輿徒于南郊，將討馮文通。

translations.literal: Summer, fifth month: a great review of chariots and conscripts was held at the southern suburb, intending to campaign against Feng Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer the army was reviewed at the southern suburb to strike Feng Wentong.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 六月庚寅，車駕伐和龍。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day gengyin: the imperial carriage campaigned against Helong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin of the sixth month the court marched on Helong.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書左僕射安原等屯于漠南，以備蠕蠕。

translations.literal: An edict that Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing An Yuan and others were to encamp in the southern desert against the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered An Yuan, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and others to camp in the southern desert against the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，兼散騎常侍鄧穎使於劉義隆。

translations.literal: On xinmao Concurrent Attendant Cadet Deng Ying was envoy to Liu Yilong.
